zh.summary: 先記住：限制不必要的資訊與操作，同時保留正常服務；改了設定，不等於已證明防護有效。

sourceBody.text: 10/27 早間：一次學一個核心概念
1. 列舉防護是什麼？
DNS、SMB、SNMP、LDAP 與 RPC 的查詢功能讓系統正常運作，也可能透露主機名稱、帳號、共享資源或服務端點。
列舉防護，就是控制「誰可以從哪裡，查到哪些資料、執行哪些操作」。
像公司的接待櫃檯：公開營業時間可以回答，內部員工資料卻不能全部交給訪客。目標不是讓所有查詢失敗，而是讓回應符合使用需求與安全政策。
2. 用在哪裡？先確認什麼？
用於已授權的資產盤點、安全檢查及設定調整。先確認：

items: 哪些來源、哪些身分需要使用？
必須提供哪些資料與操作？
哪些應公開，哪些應限制？

sourceBody.text: 公開網站查得到 DNS 記錄，通常是正常需求，不是看到資訊就能判定漏洞。例如一般 DNS 查詢與 AXFR 整區傳送是不同功能，可以保留正常解析，另行限制區域傳送對象。[RFC 5936](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5936.html#section-5)
3. 防護要分層看
第一層：服務與網路。
停用不必要功能，管理服務只讓必要來源連線。先確認依賴關係，不是看到埠就全部關掉。
第二層：身分與權限。
Authentication（身分驗證）確認你是誰；Authorization（授權）決定你可以做什麼。
Least Privilege（最小權限）只給工作所需權限。監控人員需要讀設備狀態，不代表需要修改設備設定。[NIST SP 800-53，AC-6／CM-7](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-53r5.pdf)
第三層：資料與傳輸。
限制回傳欄位、共享內容及管理物件，也保護傳輸。加密不會自動縮小查詢權限；LDAP signing 主要保護完整性，不等於加密。[Microsoft LDAP signing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/ldap-signing)
第四層：維護與監控。

維持受支援版本、修補漏洞，留下適當日誌，檢查異常查詢與權限變更。換埠或隱藏版本資訊只能輔助，不能代替真正的存取限制。[NCSC 防護指引](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/connected-places-security-principles/designing-your-connected-place/designing-your-connected-place-to-reduce-exposure)
4. 具體例子：保留監控，限制訪客
以下是合成紙上情境，沒有操作任何設備。
公司交換器需要讓管理網段的監控主機透過 SNMP 讀取狀態，訪客網段不需要這項功能。授權檢查卻發現，訪客也能查到設備名稱。
這只能證明：該來源與身分，在這次查詢中取得名稱。不能因此認定能修改設定，或已取得管理權。
管理者依需求調整來源限制與查詢權限後，要驗證兩面：

items: 不應獲准的訪客，是否仍能取得受限資訊？
應獲准的監控主機，必要查詢是否仍正常？

sourceBody.text: 如果訪客查不到，但監控也壞了，就還沒有完成符合需求的修正。這是允許與拒絕兩面的測試，不是雙因素認證。

visual.caption: 網頁補充：同時驗證限制與正常功能
visual.description: 兩項獨立檢查都要符合預期政策；這不是雙因素認證。

items.title: 訪客來源：限制資訊
items.body: 確認受限資訊未被取得，並核對規則與日誌。

items.title: 監控來源：保留功能
items.body: 確認獲准身分的必要查詢仍正常。

sourceBody.text: 5. 怎麼判讀證據？
把「設定已修改」和「實際行為已驗證」分開記錄。留下查核時間、來源、測試身分、服務、操作、回應及相關日誌；不要記錄密碼或認證秘密。
只有一筆 Timeout，最多只能說「這次沒有收到回應」。也可能是網路不通或服務故障，不能證明所有未授權存取都已阻擋。
較精確的結論是：「在本次指定來源、身分與查詢項目下，受限資訊未再被取得，必要監控仍正常。」不要把有限測試寫成整個系統絕對安全。
小檢核：
調整規則後，訪客查詢逾時。為什麼還不能宣布防護完成？請各說一項：仍要補的阻擋證據，以及正常功能檢查。
一兩句就好。12 核心＋7 選讀是本系列教學設計，不是官方固定數量。下一核心接 M05。

en.summary: Remember: restrict unnecessary information and operations while preserving normal service. Changing a setting does not establish that a defense works.

sourceBody.text: October 27 morning: one core concept at a time
1. What are enumeration countermeasures?
Query functions in DNS, SMB, SNMP, LDAP, and RPC support normal operation, but may also reveal hostnames, accounts, shared resources, or service endpoints.
Enumeration countermeasures control who can obtain which information or perform which operations, and from where.

Think of a company reception desk: public opening hours can be shared, but visitors should not receive all internal employee information. The goal is to make responses match operational needs and security policy, not to make every query fail.
2. Where are they used, and what should be established first?
They support authorized asset inventories, security reviews, and configuration changes. First establish:

items: Which sources and identities need access?
Which information and operations must be available?
What should be public, and what should be restricted?

sourceBody.text: Public DNS records for a website are usually necessary; visible information alone does not establish a vulnerability. Ordinary DNS queries and AXFR zone transfers are different functions: normal resolution can remain available while zone-transfer recipients are restricted. [RFC 5936](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5936.html#section-5)
3. Look at several layers of defense
Layer one: services and networks.
Disable unnecessary functions and allow management-service connections only from necessary sources. Check dependencies first instead of closing every visible port.
Layer two: identity and permissions.
Authentication establishes who you are; authorization determines what you may do.

Least privilege grants only the permissions needed for a task. Monitoring staff need to read device status, which does not imply a need to change device settings. [NIST SP 800-53, AC-6/CM-7](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-53r5.pdf)
Layer three: data and transport.

Restrict returned fields, shared content, and management objects, and protect transport. Encryption does not automatically narrow query permissions; LDAP signing primarily protects integrity and is not encryption. [Microsoft LDAP signing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/ldap-signing)
Layer four: maintenance and monitoring.

Use supported versions, patch vulnerabilities, retain appropriate logs, and review unusual queries and permission changes. Changing ports or hiding version information can only supplement real access restrictions. [NCSC guidance](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/connected-places-security-principles/designing-your-connected-place/designing-your-connected-place-to-reduce-exposure)
4. A concrete example: preserve monitoring, restrict guests
This is a synthetic tabletop scenario. No device was operated.

A company switch needs to let a monitoring host on the management network read status through SNMP. The guest network does not need this function. An authorized review nevertheless finds that guests can query the device name.
This establishes only that this source and identity obtained the name in this query. It does not establish permission to change settings or administrator access.
After adjusting source restrictions and query permissions to match requirements, the administrator must verify both sides:

items: Can guests who should not have access still obtain restricted information?
Can the monitoring host that should have access still perform necessary queries?

sourceBody.text: If guests can no longer query but monitoring is also broken, the correction does not yet meet requirements. These are tests of allowed and denied access, not two-factor authentication.

visual.caption: Web supplement: verify restrictions and normal service
visual.description: Both independent checks must match policy; this is not two-factor authentication.

items.title: Guest source: restrict information
items.body: Check restricted information is not obtained; review rules and logs.

items.title: Monitoring source: preserve service
items.body: Check necessary queries still work for the authorized identity.

sourceBody.text: 5. How should evidence be interpreted?

Record configuration changes separately from verified behavior. Preserve the check time, source, test identity, service, operation, response, and relevant logs; do not record passwords or authentication secrets.

A single timeout establishes at most that no response was received on this attempt. Network failure or a service outage may also explain it, so it does not establish that all unauthorized access is blocked.

A more precise conclusion is: under the specified sources, identities, and query items in this test, restricted information was no longer obtained and necessary monitoring still worked. Do not describe limited tests as proof that the entire system is absolutely secure.
Quick check:
After a rule change, a guest query times out. Why is that insufficient to declare the defense complete? Name one additional piece of blocking evidence and one normal-function check.
One or two sentences are enough. The 12 core concepts plus seven optional topics are this series' teaching design, not an official fixed count. The next core concept belongs to M05.
